newsitem.title: JAPAN: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Oct 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Oct 16.

text.p: Nissan Motor Co Ltd will power electric cars with a nickel-hydrogen battery, to be supplied by a joint venture of four companies, including Toyota Motor Corp and Matsushita Electric Industrial Co Ltd.

Two funds, which were set up to help wind up seven failed housing loan companies, are expected to invest 1.7 trillion yen in the bond market from the end of October. This move is expected to be a factor in lowering long-term interest rates.
Idemitsu Kosan Co Ltd and Showa Shell Sekiyu KK plan to raise oil and gas prices from November due to high crude prices and the weaker yen.

Nippon Steel Corp plans to buy concessions in two coal mine companies in Australia at a cost of several billion yen. It hopes to develop coal from 1998 and mine 3.8 million tonnes a year over five years.

Ricoh Co Ltd plans to expand its production of liquid crystal display (LCD) panels based on light, thin and durable polymer films rather than conventional glass substrates, at a factory in Kanagawa Prefecture. It hopes to sell new medium-sized LCD panels from October 1997.

The U.S. research company Dataquest Inc said world semiconductor shipments will shrink by nine percent to $137 billion in calendar 1996 from a year earlier, compared with an earlier forecast of $162.6 billion. Japan's chip shipments are expected to fall by 13.3 percent to $36.5 billion in the same period.
